corrected_value.title: Brahmin Left Versus Merchant Right: Changing Political Cleavages in 21 Western Democracies, 1948–2020

decisions.quote:
In this report we have presented the results from a replication of Gethin, Martínez-
Toledano and Piketty (GMP, 2022). We have tested the computational reproducibility and
robustness replicability of the GMP main results. Our replication has been limited in the
sense that we have only focused on the paper’s main result and only in the form of
additional robustness tests. Based on our analyses, we conclude that the GMP main
results are reproducible and robust to our replications.



References

Gethin, A., Martínez-Toledano, C., and Piketty, T. (2022). Brahmin Left versus Merchant
      Right: Changing Political Cleavages in 21 Western Democracies, 1948–2020. The
      Quarterly Journal of Economics, 137(1), 1–48.
decisions.location: Section 4. Conclusion and References, p. 8 (PDF p. 10), lines 427-440
decisions.reason: The report explicitly re-tests Gethin, Martínez-Toledano, and Piketty's QJE article 'Brahmin Left versus Merchant Right: Changing Political Cleavages in 21 Western Democracies, 1948–2020' (published online in 2021 with DOI 10.1093/qje/qjab036 and in print in 2022 in QJE 137(1), 1–48). Both the shipped row and blind target 0 identify this exact original paper.

decisions.quote:
With the exception of a very minor issue in the codes, we are able to run the full replication
package provided by the authors, and we find the GMP results to be fully reproducible.
Naturally, our robustness replications change the results somewhat, but our overall
conclusion is that the main GMP results are replicable and robust to our checks.
decisions.reason: The authors ran the original replication package and, after fixing one minor convergence stop for Belgium in results-all-1-region.do, obtained the original results in full. Under the codebook, obtaining the reported numbers after a minor script correction is 'computationally reproducible', confirming both the shipped and blind coding.

decisions.quote:
In this report we have presented the results from a replication of Gethin, Martínez-
Toledano and Piketty (GMP, 2022). We have tested the computational reproducibility and
robustness replicability of the GMP main results. Our replication has been limited in the
sense that we have only focused on the paper’s main result and only in the form of
additional robustness tests. Based on our analyses, we conclude that the GMP main
results are reproducible and robust to our replications.
decisions.reason: Across all five alternative specifications (restricting to core left/right parties, top 20% vs. bottom 80% cutoffs, weighting country averages by population, omitting individual control variables, and adding country fixed effects) as well as removing ex-post recoding adjustments in the do-files, the authors explicitly conclude that the main GMP results remain robust.

decisions.quote:
In this replication, we test the computational reproducibility and robustness replicability of
the main GMP results. First, we test the reproducibility of the results using the replication
package provided by the authors. Second, we test the replicability of the results through
the following robustness tests: i) restricting the sample to “core” left and right parties, ii)
analyzing top 20% versus bottom 80%, iii) weighting by population, iv) dropping control
variables, and v) using country fixed effects. Finally, we also do a replication exercise
where we test to what extent the GMP results are affected by some ex-post recoding that
we noticed when going through the authors’ do-files.
decisions.reason: The paper re-analyzes the original study's dataset and code from its replication package (with external World Bank population figures used only as country weights on the original macro estimates in one sensitivity check, not a new sample of elections or voters). Under the codebook, re-analyzing the original study's own data and code for computational reproducibility and robustness is a 'reproduction'.
